links.reason: Both verses use a painting, but NKK28 has a merchant show a portrait (படத்துருக் காட்டினான்) while MM5 has a prince briefly mistake a living girl for a painting and then 'தெளிந்து' she is real; the two make no incompatible claim, so this is not a tension, and 'desire shaped by a seen form' is not what MM5 lines 1-8 say.

1164 does build the lie on மழையினோடு இருளுங் காற்றும், and 1157 does describe the storm, but the verse 1157 never mentions a god or rescue; the god and the alibi come from the plot, so the shared image is thin and the better type is a plot development.

1183 sorts war into மனுடம், தெய்வம், இருமை and 1185 settles on மக்களோடு மக்கட்போர், which does choose one branch; but the two are adjacent verses of one speech, and 1183 lines 3-4 are admitted to be hard, so 'the lecture serves the decision' is mostly sequence.

The mother's வேலோய்... குறுமறி யொன்று கொன்றே... பலி கொடுப்ப is answered at 139 by என்னுயிர் நீத்த வேனும் யானுயிர்க்கு உறுதி சூழாது, so the king's refusal directly refutes the offered remedy; a real claim and its answer.

782 does have the companions offer மார்பங் கீற்றுப்பட்டு அழகிதாகக் கிடக்க, and K776 reckons days without விழுப்புண் wasted, so the aesthetic turn is real; but the epic verse never says the scar is a record of a day not wasted, so the first gains clause is supplied, not found.

K967 is about living by following those who scorn one (ஒட்டார்பின் சென்று வாழ்தலின் கெட்டான் எனப்படுதல் நன்று); Civakan in 1152 refuses life through his wife's விஞ்சை, which is neither following enemies nor a reputation claim, and the 'male friend's help' clause is not in either text.

2477 describes only the bride after the night (துவண்ட கொம்பின் பொற்பினள்); it never mentions நாண் or நிறை, so the claim that shame falls here lawfully 'without the loss the Kural fears' is read into the verse.

K773 makes ஊராண்மை the edge of valour when the foe is struck by misfortune, and 2258 has Nabulan, seeing the king's eyes flicker, hold his blow, laugh and say நீ யஞ்சல் ... காய்ந்திலேன்; நாணி names the striker's own shame as motive, which the couplet leaves unsaid.
links.text_issue: line 1 ஏந்தறன் is read, not certain

links.reason: 2988 only calls the wives to cross தொல்வினை; it does not say it is by the seeker's effort alone or deny a fire, and Tm219 is a fire-rite (அங்கி உதிக்க... வினை சுடும்); 'Jain effort versus Saiva rite' is the marker's frame, not a claim the two verses contradict. 2846 would be the true contrast.

The sage's explanation of a past vow (NKK150 அந்த நோன்பு) and Devanthi's reported claim of a broken vow (SK9 பொய்த்தாய் பழம்பிறப்பில்) share a pattern, not an image; Devanthi's claim is only reported and the poem later gives another cause, so 'the epics do not tie past deeds to suffering alone' is only a shared theme.

982 shows modesty holding her (நாணின்று விலக்க) while she melts, which does add inner feeling to K1094's outward look-down/smile; but the verse has no looking away and back, so 'lacks the timing' is not a gain the verse supplies.

Both verses show a king crowning another and putting on ascetic dress (முனிவனாய் நின்றான் / பண்ணவர் படிவம் கொண்டான்); the verse UKK23 says nothing of childlessness, so the contrast 'follows childlessness' is not in the Tamil and qualifies does not fit.

95 shows her heart flowing to the song (பண்ணினுக் கொழுகு நெஞ்சின்) and மதிமயக்கு, but there is no guarded chamber or stable in the verse, so the Kural's confinement-versus-நிறை frame is imported; the note describes a scene the verse does not state.

1292 is explicitly மீட்டும் கொளப்பட்டாள் after 1290's venom leaves, so the second answers the first; but there is no incompatible claim here, only a conceit turning cure into the next bite, so this is a development, not a tension.

204 describes only union (பவளச் செவ்வாய் அமிர்து உண்டு); the quarrel and making-up are said to lie in 201-203, which are not in view, so the claim of the sequence rests on other verses and a second wife and flattery are not in this verse.

691 has the king's men say நம் படை இரு முறை உடைந்தபின், which refers back to the hunters' rout in 436 (வாட்படை அனுங்க வேடர்... பகழியால் வீட்டினார்); the later verse is the army's own telling of the earlier fight.
1851 says wrongdoers sow the seed of evil deeds (வித்து மாட்டி) and perish, and 1939 shows the harvest with the sage's வினையின் விளைவே; the later verse fulfils the earlier in the same விளை- image.
164 lists the seven kings and 165 says they refuse tribute and march; this is plot order, which the graph already records, and the 'stratagem necessary' reading adds little the verses state.

Both verses set Civakan beside the Murugan figure while the speakers are unsure (1948 வேள்கொலோ... மைந்தனோ; 812 மஞ்ஞையே முருகன் தான்), once as the kings' terror and once as the women's desire; the shared image is meaningful and the note is accurate.

Thirikadugam 12 defines வேளாளன் as விருந்திருக்க உண்ணாதான், and K81 says household life is for விருந்தோம்பி வேளாண்மை; the verse fixes the vel- name by hospitality alone, which develops the couplet's term.

866 has learned men judging the hour (முகோரை... மூர்த்தம் நோக்கி), while CC1344 only says கணி fixed the day and then the cord is tied; cross-epic shared theme of an auspicious hour, with no development, and 866's last words are uncertain.

1876 says she guarded the blame (பட்டபழி காத்து) by sending Taran off with a false word (தூது பிற சொல்லி), which tests K56's சொற்காத்து against truth-telling, a case the couplet does not foresee; both gains clauses hold.

3133 says fasting and meditation wash off evil deeds (தீவினை கழுஉம்), and Nal51 first agrees (தவத்தின்முன் நில்லாதாம் பாவம்) then limits it with நல்வினை தீர்விடத்து; so Nal51 qualifies the verse, not the other way, and the 'company carried the austerity to their deaths' clause is not in 3133.

31 only describes sugarcane and paddy fields, 44 only ploughmen driving buffalo; there is no claim or contrast between them, and 'Soolamani leaves the crop alone' is just the absence of a figure in one verse.

Soolamani 927 is a literal scene of a tamer refitting ropes (புரைசை... புதுவடம்); Tm2023 is a metaphor of five elephants in the body (ஆக மதத்தன ஐந்து களிறு); a keeper and an elephant are generic and the verse does not dwell on the tamer's skill or its failure.

2965 shows women beating bangles at the king's going; Tm157 shows wives and kin turning back (ஊர்த்துறைக் காலே ஒழிவர்) at the bier; the contrast of a living departure with a death is real but the Tm verse gives the epic's grief no 'Saiva reading', so the gains are overstated.

2846's கூடிய மும்மை blazes and burns the வினைமரம் with no god, while Tm117 says the சூரியகாந்தம் burns the cotton only in சூரியன் சந்நிதி; on the reading of the sun as the Lord this is release by one's own virtues versus by grace, a real incompatible claim.

486 shows women giving their hearts to princes (நெஞ்சு தாழ் ஒரீஇ... மாலுமாகி), but Nal17 warns a man off a woman's வேல்கண் for her age; the epic verse carries no warning or beauty-of-the-woman claim, so the pair is thematic and the gains are largely supplied.

332 has the beasts fail to say கொடிதே காதலிப் பிரிதல், and 333 has the birds fail to say யாம் துணைபுணர்ந்து உறைதும் யாங்குப் பிரிந்து உறைதி; the pair truly shows precept then example, though the pair is better read as parallel than as one extending the other.

K926 condemns drink (நஞ்சுண்பார் கள்ளுண்பவர்) and K1201 says காமம் is sweeter than கள்; the second only uses liquor as a measure of sweetness and never praises drinking, so there are no incompatible claims, the 'tension' is only a shared word.

156's promise (தருவன் நீ இழந்த தேவி) and 152's hope (திருப்பவும் மீட்கலாம்) are both about the lost queen, but the claim that the deceit 'works because it answers his grief' relies on verse 155 and a reconstructed plot, and both verses are marked uncertain.

1053's content is admitted to be lost in broken grammar (the petition to the moon is not read), so 'to beg the moon to bring tomorrow near' is a reconstruction; 1056 only says the moon shrank and set (மெல்லவே மெல்லவே சுருங்கி), so the link depends on that guess.

139's king refuses to take a life (மன்னுயிர்க்கு அரணம்) and 175's Yasomathi beats the dog (நாயை எற்றினன்) without knowing; the second is irony on the first, not an incompatible claim, and only one verse (175) is read for what the dog is; better as qualifies.

316's deity foretells the prince will crush the hostile king, and 1809's friends say a life has come that will be கூற்றமாய் to the கீழ்மகன் who seized the land, with கருமம் விளைந்தவா; the prophecy and its working out, though 'armed men' is an addition.

Soolamani 200 gives the refuge in the Lord's feet (அடிகளே சரணம்) and CC380 has Civakan taking refuge in அறிவரன் as ஊழ்வினை துரத்தலானும் உணர்வு...; both are the same Jain doctrine, but 'qualifies' overstates a mere parallel and 200 is uncertain.

2124 has the women say நின்னடை கற்ற எமக்கு... மெல்ல நடமோ and 2125 has others scold பிடியலை பாவி for a rough gait; the playful inversion of the she-elephant figure is real, but it is a continuation within one scene, not an incompatible claim.

2412 is a bath scene with instruments (முழங்கின இன்னிய); it has no hint of a reversal, no bridegroom named, and the 'hero who will later fear kingship' is outside the verse, so Nal23's warning of மணப்பறை/பிணப்பறை is imposed.

45 says kin scorn the ruined (பெரிது இகழ்ந்து), and 44 argues for crossing the wasteland for wealth for kin; the pair works only by the editor's order of fragments and an unnamed speaker, and 'no claim of his on them' is not said.
links.text_issue: 44 sense uncertain; fragments in editor's order

links.reason: Soolamani 686 offers a cobra's hood-jewel (அரவின் அரழற்படமுடை மணி) and Pur73 a blind man stumbling on a sleeping tiger (துஞ்சு புலி இடறிய சிதடன்); the two images differ, so it is the same logic (a fool provoking the strong), and the claim that the epic lacks the king's gentler half is not a gain the epic side receives.

The patikam has the Vidyadhara king's daughter losing at the vina (வீணையில் தோற்ற ஆறும்) while 619 has the companion saying the kings will drown in her music; the forecast is overturned by the announced outcome, a real claim-and-refutation within the epic.

1155's flatterers say no god or man matches him (வானவர் இவற்கு மாறாய் வருபவர் மதிப்பின் இல்லை) and 770 says the lion was beyond the gods; both are hyperbole above gods, but 'the story means to test the two claims against each other' is not shown in either verse.

297 says through உயிர்க்கொலை வினைக்கொடுமை they fell into animals and pain, matching 63's the youth's claim of births of pain from harm to living bodies; but 297 only begins to name the beasts and does not name the act, so the note overstates what the muni 'names'.

2998 has Civakan board a சிவிகை that the gods bear away, and Tm153 has the lord of the land mount the காட்டுச் சிவிகை with drums before him; a king's last ride in a palanquin is shared, but the epic verse does not make the palanquin a bier, so the pairing is a contrast the reader brings.
links.text_issue: 2998 uses the same vehicle word as a different thing
